title: DistDNA: Language Model Fingerprinting under Stochastic Decoding
abstract: arXiv:2611.27831v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Behavioral fingerprints identify a large language model (LLM) from its responses to a shared set of prompts, enabling applications such as verifying whether a deployed model corresponds to the checkpoint it claims to be. Deployed models, however, are commonly served with stochastic decoding, under which the same model may produce different responses to an identical prompt, depending on an unknown temperature and top-$p$ setting. Existing representations such as LLM DNA provide limited treatment of this variation. A natural remedy is to characterize models by their response distributions, which, however, raises two challenges. First, each distribution must be estimated from only a small number of sampled responses. Second, a change in decoding setting can alter responses to the same extent as a change of checkpoint. translated_title: DistDNA：随机解码下的语言模型指纹识别
translated_abstract: 行为指纹通过大语言模型（LLM）对一组共享提示的响应来识别该模型，可支持诸如验证已部署模型是否与其声称的检查点相符等应用。然而，已部署的模型通常采用随机解码提供服务，此时同一模型对相同提示可能产生不同的响应，且温度和 top-p 设置往往是未知的。诸如 LLM DNA 之类的现有表示方法对这种变化的处理能力有限。一种自然的解决方案是通过模型的响应分布来刻画模型，但这带来了两个挑战：首先，每个分布只能从少量采样响应中估计；其次，解码设置的改变可能以与更换检查点相当的程度改变响应。因此，仅凭指纹距离无法为模型身份提供完整的判断依据，识别通常还需依赖……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出 DistDNA 方法，通过从少量采样响应中估计响应分布，并将解码设置变化与检查点变化的影响区分开来，实现随机解码条件下的大语言模型可靠指纹识别。
en_tdlr: DistDNA enables reliable LLM fingerprinting under stochastic decoding by estimating response distributions from a small number of sampled responses and disentangling the effects of decoding-setting changes from checkpoint changes.
